prompt:
Write 7 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim, in time order. Injury: wrist fracture. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1260; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- Years ago the patient had a small strain in the same area that healed fully.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: First notice of loss received from the claimant describing a rear-end collision at a low-speed intersection. The claimant reports a wrist fracture and states the claimant was driving the insured vehicle at the time of impact. The driver is named on the policy, and the claim has been opened for review.

Entry 2: Spoke with the claimant by phone to confirm the sequence of events. The account given matches what was described at first notice, and the claimant was consistent on every point discussed, including the direction of travel and the vehicle position at impact.

Entry 3: Police report obtained and reviewed. It confirms the claimant was in the vehicle at the scene. No independent witnesses were identified in the report or during follow-up calls, so the account rests on the parties and the photos.

Entry 4: Reviewed photographs submitted by the claimant. They confirm several details of the collision, and the damage to the rear of the vehicle is mostly in line with the described impact. No earlier damage to the vehicle is known from prior claims or inspection notes.

Entry 5: Medical records received. The reported wrist fracture is consistent in kind and force with a rear-end impact of this type. Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the claimant improved. Records also note a minor strain in the same area years ago, which healed fully and does not appear to affect the current claim.

Entry 6: Checked the coverage history. Nothing suggests the damage occurred before the policy coverage began, and the policy period covers the date of loss.

Entry 7: Claim assessment updated. The collision and injury appear to be genuine and consistent with the evidence available. Next step is to finalize the medical bill review and send the claimant a settlement letter, since the claimant is not represented.
